content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm currently working with a [company_name] [product_name]. This device needs to communicate with another device using Modbus TCP. I've been trying to set up the connection, but I am not receiving any data from the [product_name] during a virtual communication check. The [product_name] should operate as a slave for the other device. Does anyone have advice or examples on how to create successful Modbus communication? The specific [product_name] I am using is: [article_no] Looking forward to your responses. Kind regards, [user_name]
Could you specify which type of Modbus device is being used?

Hi, As mentioned, your [product_name] is a recent model [version_no]. Please make sure you are using [product_name] [version_no], which you likely already have. For testing purposes, I usually use ModScan, a simulator available for 30 days, which can function as a slave or master. Within [product_name], set up Modbus communication by going to: Tools -> Ethernet Connections -> enable 'Allow Modbus access,' and then create a client or server connection according to your requirements. I've attached an address table to help identify which variables can be read or written. Hope this is helpful, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to set up Modbus TCP communication between a [company_name] [product_name] and an external device, with the [product_name] configured as a slave. There is some uncertainty around properly enabling Modbus mode and accessing variables. Users are also seeking clarity on which software versions and specific settings are required for successful integration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear instructions for setting up Modbus slave mode on the [product_name], plus reliable communication with the external device and practical examples to guide the process.
